zara-cust: Hey team — since ~09:10 UTC we're seeing a sudden spike in 429s and elevated latency on our dedicated pool for tenant acme-corp. ~30% of /v1/generate requests returning 429. Any idea?

mike: Hi @zara-cust — sorry about that. Can you paste a sample curl you used (headers) and one of the X-Redwood-Req or x-request-id values from a 429 response? Also which dedicated pool name you expect?

zara-cust: Sure — here's the minimal repro we tried:

  curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \\n       -H "X-Redwood-Tier: gold " \\n       -H "X-Redwood-Tenant: acme-corp" \\n       https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'

Response headers had x-request-id: r12345 and returned HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests. The dedicated pool name should be dedicated-gold-01.

mike: Thanks — forwarding. @samg can you take a look at r12345 trace?

samg: Looking. Quick sanity: the tier header has a trailing space in that curl: "X-Redwood-Tier: gold ". I'm seeing in the control-plane logs that our routing parser is triggering a fallback route when header parsing yields a trailing-empty token. Suspect bug in legacy header-array/CSV parsing that treats "gold " as two tokens ("gold", "") and then the selector falls through to a fallback matching rule that points to our hot/shared pool.

samg: Grab from trace (sanitized):

```
[2026-03-17T09:11:02Z] req=r12345 tenant=acme-corp tier_header='gold ' raw_tokens=['gold','']
[2026-03-17T09:11:02Z] selector: trying exact_match('gold') -> miss
[2026-03-17T09:11:02Z] selector: trying fallback_regex('^gold.*') -> hit -> route=hotpool-1
[2026-03-17T09:11:02Z] routed to hotpool-1 (shared) -> rate_limit=100rps exceeded -> 429
```

samg: So the core issue: parser creates an empty token from trailing whitespace/comma cases and the selector path accidentally prefers a regex-based fallback before confirming exact pool affinity. That results in misrouting to hot pool and subjecting the request to shared rate limits.

zara-cust: Ok — makes sense. Any quick workaround?

samg: Short-term options: 1) Ensure requests don't send trailing whitespace (fix client) — removing the trailing space in X-Redwood-Tier immediately fixes routing. 2) If you can, add header `X-Redwood-Route: pool:dedicated-gold-01` to force-pinned routing. 3) I can temporarily add an override for tenant=acme-corp to prefer dedicated-gold-01 on our control plane until we ship the patch.

mike: @zara-cust want us to add the override?

zara-cust: Please add the override if it's quick — we have production traffic.

samg: Will do. Also filing a code fix: tighten the CSV/header parser (trim tokens, drop empty tokens), and change selector ordering to prefer exact key matches before regex/fallbacks. Plan: PR #4321, canary deploy tomorrow AM UTC, full rollout after monitoring.

deploy-bot: PR #4321 (control-plane: strict-header-parse + selector-order) queued for canary at 2026-03-18T02:00:00Z.

samg: Also adding short-lived rate-limit exemption for tenant acme-corp on hotpool-1 to avoid immediate 429s while override applied. Will remove after patch.

mike: Thanks. Zara — can you confirm removing the trailing whitespace on your client now and we can validate?

zara-cust: Confirmed — removed trailing space and 429s stopped. Latency back to normal. Thanks for the quick triage :relieved:

mike: Following up on billing/overage separately — will keep thread updated once patch rolls.

samg: I'll post the PR link and ETA for canary results in this thread once scheduled.

mike: Closing loop once patch is live. Thanks everyone.
